members.duties: mechanics audit: damage-budget compliance (flat numbers on Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21), prereq shapes (Adept exactly 2, Master exactly 3), cost math (cards 2/4/8), level gates, dice remnants, stale vocabulary, cross-chapter contradictions
consistency and voice: repeated phrases, tonal drift, name collisions, redundant sections, flavor-vs-rules balance
final quality: structure, cross-references, missing content, completeness
presentation: Quarto/Typst render, heading hierarchy, table formatting/overflow, typography, page flow, card layout, reference-sheet usability, em-dash law

payload.name: hol-rulebook
payload.problem_domain: Heroes of Legend TTRPG rulebook chapter review and disposition

payload.statement:
Chapter under review: ch13 (quarto-book/chapters/13-combat.qmd), "Combat", 457 lines.

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files a finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope

Findings cite [file:line] in the chapter. Mechanics findings state the broken
value and the expected value. Cross-chapter checks use the authoritative
chapters as the reference, not this chapter.

Disposition classes (for the librarian's synthesis):
  mechanical    - safe to implement as a micro-PR (headings, tables, wording,
                  em-dashes, single-cell refs, budget rows)
  substantive   - needs a dispatched implementation pass (multi-file, new content)
  design-decision - needs Bruce's ruling; implement the recommended default,
                  flagged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md

Standing book conventions are in force: zero em-dashes in book text; damage
budgets flat at Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21; card costs 2/4/8;
Adept prereqs exactly 2, Master exactly 3. Violations of these conventions
are findings, not questions.

payload.argument: The chapter presents itself as a complete combat engine: attacks that always connect resolved by a single roll, all dice in player hands, tiered damage and defense, plus conditions, morale, a wound system, and two fully worked examples. The lenses should probe three layers: internal table consistency (tier bands, condition costs, wound-roll ranges), cross-chapter agreement (example card figures, costs, and prereq counts against the cards and core chapters and the standing budget conventions), and editorial hygiene (cross-references, pagebreaks, punctuation conventions). It does not hold as written. The wound table's printed ranges overlap its own special-triple rows, so one roll can match two entries; standing up is priced as a maneuver in one table, as movement in another, and as half movement in the example; and the surprise penalty applies to the first roll in one passage but the whole first round in another. A disposition plan must therefore carry a mechanical pass for those three (carve the special triples out of the ranges, pick one resource cost for standing up and align all three sites, unify the surprise wording), a substantive pass reconciling the example's damage figures and card costs against the cards chapter and the flat damage budgets, and a short design-decision list for DA-rule gaps: defense-roll criticals and fumbles, the fractional Challenge-to-penalty mapping, and stating the minimum-one damage floor as a rule rather than only showing it in the example. On the positive side, every arithmetic step in both examples checks out against the stated tier thresholds, the design rationale is consistent, and the em-dash convention is clean; the refute is scoped to targeted corrections, not a rewrite.

evidence.claim: The wound table's printed ranges overlap its special-triple rows, so a single roll can match two entries.
Standing up costs a Maneuver in the basic-maneuvers table but movement in the conditions table and the worked example.
The surprise penalty is scoped to the first roll in the prose but to the first round in the modifiers table.
The minimum-one damage floor after armor appears only inside the worked example, never as a stated rule in this chapter.
The example's Basic Melee figures need reconciliation against the cards chapter and the flat damage-budget convention.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: His Basic Melee card deals 2 on Standard

evidence.claim: The combat example catches its own rules mistake mid-sentence, reading like an editor's note left in the text.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: but wait, Kael is only Adept

evidence.claim: Attack and death-save tables define critical and fumble overrides, but the defense table defines neither, leaving defense rolls without special results.
Every arithmetic step in both worked examples checks out against the stated tier thresholds, supporting overall mechanical coherence.

payload.argument: Refute: the chapter's mechanics break cross-chapter numbers and book conventions in multiple places. MECHANICAL (micro-PR cells): (1) [13-combat:371] the Knight's Standard damage is stated as 3, but the bestiary Knight block (ch20:90) lists Longsword 6/9/12, so the expected value is 9; corrected math drops Kael to 5 HP, rippling through [13-combat:391] and [13-combat:419]. (2) [13-combat:381] Dark Bolt Standard is stated as 3 necrotic; the bestiary Cultist (ch20:88) budgets 2/4/6, expected 4, so Lyra ends round 1 at 6 HP, not 7 (also lines 391 and 419). (3) [13-combat:357] the buckler is given +2 DR; the armor chapter (ch16:70) grants +1 DR, so the totals at [13-combat:371] should be DR 3. (4) [13-combat:353] Gust at Standard knocks the cultist Prone, but the spell card (ch11:310) makes Standard a 10 ft push with Prone only on Strong; the stand-up beat at [13-combat:377] is therefore invalid. (5) [13-combat:63] Stand Up costs a Maneuver while [13-combat:182] and [13-combat:377] treat standing as movement. (6) [13-combat:124] Surprised is 'first round only' while [13-combat:192] and the glossary (ch21:147) say first roll. (7) [13-combat:122] lists cover as a +1/+3 defense bonus while [13-combat:327-328] state a -1/-3 attacker penalty with no cross-reference (book convention per ch21:149, ch22:134-136). (8) [13-combat:175] Frozen imposes Incapacitated yet is ended by spending an action the victim cannot take. (9) [13-combat:176] Grappled/Restrained cite an 'Escape action' that no table defines. (10) [13-combat:303-311] wound ranges 200-265, 300-365, 500-565 numerically contain the separately listed triples 222/333/555. (11) [13-combat:441] 'damage die' is a dice remnant in a dice-free damage system. (12) [13-combat:439] claims four-to-one odds while only three party members are demonstrated. SUBSTANTIVE (dispatched pass): [13-combat:234] 'Dual Wielder', [13-combat:389] 'Menacing Glare' (also skill-rank-gated, off-model per ch05:444 and ch07:90), and [13-combat:411] 'Flurry' name cards that exist nowhere in the book; either add them to ch09 or rewrite the examples. DESIGN-DECISION (Bruce's ruling): [13-combat:361/387/409] 'plate armor: DR 4' matches the bestiary Knight (ch20:90) but contradicts the armor chapter's plate DR 6 (ch16:94, ch06:69); the example's math survives either fix because the minimum-1 floor keeps every hit at 1.

evidence.claim: The Knight's Standard-tier damage in the worked example is 3, but the bestiary Knight (Challenge 3) carries Longsword 6/9/12 so Standard must be 9; with corrected buckler DR the blow deals 6 and Kael ends at 5 HP, changing lines 371, 391, 419.
Dark Bolt is budgeted 2/4/6 in the bestiary cultist entry, so a Standard hit is 4, not the 3 used here; Lyra should sit at 6 HP after round 1 and the summaries at 391 and 419 must follow.
Gust's Standard tier only pushes 10 ft per the arcane spell card; Prone arrives at Strong, so the cultist should not be knocked down and the later stand-up beat cannot happen.
The buckler grants +1 DR in the armor chapter; the example's +2 is the shield's value, so the stated DR totals must drop to 3.
Standing from Prone is movement in the conditions table and the example (half move), contradicting the basic-maneuvers table which charges a Maneuver.
Dual Wielder, Menacing Glare, and Flurry appear only in this chapter; full-book searches find no such cards, and gating an ability on a skill rank contradicts the Discipline-gating model.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Dual Wielder talent, which removes that restriction.

evidence.claim: The wound table ranges numerically contain the special triples listed as separate rows, so rolls of 222, 333, and 555 fall in two cells at once; ranges should exclude the triple rows.
Cover appears twice with opposite sign conventions - a +1/+3 defense bonus versus a -1/-3 attacker penalty - with no cross-reference; the book-wide convention is the attacker penalty.
The ambush epilogue credits a high roll on a damage die, but the game uses flat damage with no damage dice anywhere in the book.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: rolled high on a damage die.

evidence.claim: The Knight wears plate at DR 4, matching the bestiary block but contradicting the armor chapter's plate DR 6; label and value must be reconciled book-wide.
Frozen imposes Incapacitated yet is ended by spending an action the victim cannot take, and the grapple conditions cite an Escape action no table defines.

Worked-math audit: Kael Strong 4 minus Knight DR 4 floors at 1 (matches); Knight Standard 9 minus Kael DR 3 equals 6 (chapter says 1); Dark Bolt Standard 4 unarmored (chapter says 3); Ember Lance Standard 4 plus 2 pass-through match the card; Basic Melee 1/2/3 plus Brawn matches the ch09 card; initiative, grapple, stealth, and morale rolls all recompute correctly.

payload.argument: Evidence shows the chapter's rule framework and its cross-references largely hold: the Critical-table, always-hit, and players-roll-all references to core-resolution all resolve; Riposte's Reaction trigger, Basic Melee's 1/2/3+Brawn values, Ember Lance's Standard 4, the Light-property list, the surprise/Stealth-vs-passive-Insight formula, and the grapple rules all match their authoritative sources. But the flagship full-round worked example contradicts the bestiary on two monster stat blocks (Knight Standard damage priced at 3 vs 9 per its 6/9/12 longsword; Cultist Dark Bolt at 3 vs 4 per its 2/4/6), grants Gust a Prone effect its card reserves for Strong, adds Brawn instead of Agility to a Finesse off-hand shortsword, and rests three beats on cards the book never defines anywhere (Flurry, Menacing Glare, Dual Wielder). The D666 wound table strands its two most severe rows (600-633, 634-665) with no achievable rolls and double-claims 222, 333, and 555 across two rows each. The disposition plan must therefore rest on: a substantive rewrite of the worked example to align every number with the bestiary stat blocks and card text; a ruling on whether to add the three phantom cards or replace those beats with existing cards (e.g., Cyclone or Power Strike); a re-mapped D666 wound table where every row is reachable and no outcome is double-claimed; and mechanical unification of the cover modifiers and the stand-up-from-prone cost.

evidence.claim: The worked example prices the Knight's Standard hit at 3 damage, but the bestiary stat block (20-bestiary.qmd, Knight Challenge 3) lists its longsword at 6/9/12 (Weak/Standard/Strong), so a Standard defense result should deal 9, reduced by DR 4 to 5 — not minimum-1 — which rewrites Kael's HP ledger (11 to 6, not 10) and the round's damage totals.

The example gives the Cultist's Dark Bolt 3 necrotic on Standard, but the bestiary Cultist entry (20-bestiary.qmd) lists Dark Bolt at 2/4/6 necrotic, so Standard should be 4; Lyra should drop from 10 to 6 HP, not 7.

The example has a Standard Gust roll knock the cultist Prone, but the Gust card (11-arcane-spells.qmd) pushes 10 ft on Standard and grants Prone only on Strong; the subsequent 'stands up from Prone' beat is built on that error.

The example frames Flurry as a Master maneuver Kael cannot use, yet no Flurry card exists anywhere in the book (grep of all chapters); the beat teaches a restriction on a card the book never presents.

Menacing Glare is presented as an Intimidation Adept ability that forces a Morale Check, but no such card exists in any chapter, and Intimidation is a skill (07-skills.qmd, Brawn-keyed), not a Discipline, so the morale beat has no rule backing.

The two-weapon rule says the Dual Wielder talent lifts the Light-property restriction, but no Dual Wielder talent exists in the classes or talents chapters; the restriction is unconditional as the book stands.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: unless you have the Dual Wielder talent

evidence.claim: D666 (three sorted dice) yields exactly 56 achievable outcomes; enumerated, the ranges 600-633 (Crippling Blow) and 634-665 (Shattered Spirit) contain zero achievable rolls — the two most severe wounds can never occur — while 222, 333, and 555 each sit inside two rows (200-265/222, 300-365/333, 500-565/555), so the table both strands its severest entries and double-claims three outcomes.

Cover is implemented twice in the same chapter with opposite signs: the defense-modifiers table grants +1 to +3 from cover, while the Cover table imposes -1/-3 on the attacker's roll; because players make all rolls and enemies never roll attacks, the two tables cannot both be applied to the same incoming attack.

The off-hand shortsword carries the Finesse property (15-equipment.qmd), so per Basic Melee the off-hand damage should add Agility (+2) rather than Brawn (+1), making the example's two-weapon total 6, not 5.

Rising from prone is costed three different ways within the chapter: a Maneuver (basic-maneuvers Stand Up), a move (conditions-table 'Stand up (move)'), and half movement (worked example), and no other chapter settles the cost.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Cultist 1 stands up from Prone (uses half his movement)

payload.argument: Refute: voice and consistency must change before this chapter stands as a publishable unit. Overall tone is on-register with the rest of the book (punchy second-person, deliberate motifs like the always-hit slogan and the roll-once refrain), and the em-dash ban is honored (no U+2014 in the file), but the chapter fails on cross-chapter naming and internal restatement. Findings: (1) Phantom references - the worked example invokes a morale maneuver gated on an Intimidation Discipline (13-combat.qmd:389, 405), but no such ability exists in the weapon-maneuvers chapter and Intimidation is a skill, not a Discipline (07-skills; 14-social-conflict.qmd:27); Flurry (13-combat.qmd:411) and the Dual Wielder talent (13-combat.qmd:234) likewise appear nowhere else in the book. Disposition: substantive if the abilities are added to 09-talents-abilities; mechanical if the examples are rewritten with existing cards. (2) Draft residue - 13-combat.qmd:411 retains a first-person editorial aside that must be excised; 13-combat.qmd:9 carries a stale art-tracker descriptor out of format with every other chapter's caption convention. Disposition: mechanical. (3) Example-vs-card value drift - a Standard Gust knocks the target Prone (13-combat.qmd:353) though the card grants Prone only on Strong (11-arcane-spells.qmd:306-311); Dark Bolt Standard damage is quoted as 3 (13-combat.qmd:381) against the bestiary's 4 (20-bestiary.qmd:88); the Knight's Standard damage is 3 (13-combat.qmd:371, 391) against the bestiary's longsword values (20-bestiary.qmd:90). Disposition: mechanical (align example numbers to the cards). (4) Equipment-value drift - the example's buckler grants +2 DR (13-combat.qmd:357, 371) but the armor and equipment chapters rate bucklers at +1 (16-armor-shields.qmd:70; 15-equipment.qmd:91); plate armor is DR 4 in the example and bestiary (13-combat.qmd:361; 20-bestiary.qmd:90) yet DR 6 in the armor chapter and core-resolution (16-armor-shields.qmd:40; 06-core-resolution.qmd:69). Disposition: mechanical for the buckler, design-decision for plate. (5) Internal restatement divergences - rising from Prone costs a Maneuver per the basic-maneuver table (13-combat.qmd:63), is listed as a movement action in the conditions table (13-combat.qmd:182), and costs half movement in the example (13-combat.qmd:377); Shove is Brawn vs Brawn/Agility here (13-combat.qmd:58) but an opposed Brawn check in the reference sheet (22-reference-sheets.qmd:65), and Grapple uses skill-qualified rolls (13-combat.qmd:204) against both bare-Brawn versions. Disposition: design-decision to pick one cost, mechanical to propagate. (6) Cross-chapter verbatim echo - 13-combat.qmd:113 closes with nearly the same sentence core-resolution closes with at 06-core-resolution.qmd:117. Disposition: mechanical (rephrase). (7) Callout-label drift - DA Guidance is bold at 13-combat.qmd:196 and italic at 13-combat.qmd:269, with unlabeled and differently labeled italics at 218 and 246; other chapters use the bold form (16-armor-shields.qmd:82; 19-gm-guidance.qmd:133). Disposition: mechanical. (8) Vacant vocabulary - the Choke option ends in flavor where a rule is needed (13-combat.qmd:216), since no suffocation rule exists anywhere in the book; non-lethal takedowns avoid bleeding out (13-combat.qmd:242), a death state the chapter's own dying rules never define. Disposition: design-decision to add suffocation, mechanical to rephrase. (9) Minor nits - one-off 'bloodied' (13-combat.qmd:401) beside 'hurt'/'wounded' (401, 415); mixed minus-sign characters (U+2212 at 123/302/303/310 vs plain hyphens at 192/327-328) and en-dash ranges in the wound table against hyphen ranges in every other table. Disposition: mechanical. Consistency that holds: Challenge naming, passive Insight formula (matches 21-glossary.qmd:195), Basic Melee and Ember Lance values, Catch Breath wording (matches 22-reference-sheets.qmd:68), initiative tie rule, and the house voice all match their authoritative chapters.

evidence.claim: The worked example cites a morale maneuver gated on a Discipline that does not exist anywhere else in the book; Intimidation is a skill, and no such ability appears in the maneuvers chapter.
Flurry is invoked and then rejected in an aside that reads like a first-draft self-correction, and the maneuver is absent from the authoritative talents chapter.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: but wait, Kael is only Adept. He can't use Flurry

evidence.claim: The Gust example applies a Prone knockdown on a Standard result, while the spell card reserves Prone for Strong.
The example quotes a buckler granting +2 DR, twice the rating the equipment and armor chapters assign to bucklers.
The knight's plate armor is rated DR 4 here, matching the bestiary but contradicting the armor chapter's Plate value of 6.
Rising from prone is priced three different ways within the chapter: as a Maneuver, as a movement action, and as half of movement in the example.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: stands up from Prone (uses half his movement)

evidence.claim: The chapter's rationale sentence is a near-verbatim repeat of core-resolution's closing sentence.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The only difference is whose hands are on the dice

evidence.claim: The chapter opener's art caption carries a stale descriptor unlike the class-based descriptors used by every other chapter's captions.
The Choke grapple option ends with flavor instead of a rule, and no suffocation mechanic exists anywhere else in the book.
Non-lethal takedowns are described as avoiding a bleed-out state that the chapter's own dying rules never establish.
The DA Guidance callout is bold in one place and italic in another within the same chapter, unlike the uniform bold form used elsewhere in the book.

Cross-check against authoritative chapters: Challenge naming, passive Insight formula, Basic Melee and Ember Lance values, Catch Breath wording, initiative tie rule, and the overall register all hold; no em-dashes appear in the chapter.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: matches core-resolution on Challenge naming and defense formulas

payload.argument:
Audited the chapter as rendered in the current build (quarto-book/_output/Heroes-of-Legend.pdf, built 2026-08-25; chapter 13 spans PDF pages 200-224). Five layout defects, in severity order:

1. CRITICAL - Wound Table (chapters/13-combat.qmd:297-316): the 15-row table is taller than one page, and the theme wraps every table in an unbreakable block (style.typ:212, 'block(breakable: false, it)'), so it cannot flow to the next page. On PDF p.216 the final four rows (566-599, 600-633, 634-665, 666) collapse into a single overlapping band, are clipped by the bottom margin, and the page footer overprints the table. A GM cannot read the worst four wound results - this is the money table of the Dying and Death section. Fix: remove the unbreakable wrapper and let Typst repeat the header row on page 2 (style.typ:208-216, contradicts its own comment at line 192), or split the table into two with repeated headers at chapter [13-combat:297]. The former is the mechanical, book-wide fix.

2. HIGH - Doubled table captions on all four tables (13-combat.qmd:51, 147, 162, 297): each caption hard-codes a 'Table 13.x:' label, and Quarto's crossref auto-numbering (crossref.chapters: true) prepends its own 'Table 15.x:' (15 = the chapter's rendered number). Build shows 'Table 15.4: Table 13.4: Wound Table (D666)' on p.216 and the same doubling on p.204/206/209. Fix: delete the hard-coded 'Table 13.x:' prefix from each caption line and keep only the title plus the {#tbl-...} id, so the auto number is the sole label.

3. HIGH - Literal '## Damage Types' printed as body text on p.207 (13-combat.qmd:126-127): the '## Damage Types' line directly follows the pagebreak with no blank line between them, so it is not parsed as a heading - it renders in regular body type, its hashes visible. Verified visually in the build. Consequences: the section is absent from the TOC (the Chapter 15 TOC block lists 15.1-15.15 with no Damage Types entry, confirmed in build) and the heading is invisible to any cross-reference. Fix: insert a blank line between [13-combat:126] and [13-combat:127] so the heading parses; verify the TOC picks it up on rebuild.

4. MEDIUM - Blank page 219 (13-combat.qmd:333 and 335): two consecutive pagebreaks (after Cover, before the midpoint placeholder figure) force a fully empty page into the build - p.219 contains only header and footer. Fix: delete one of the two pagebreak lines [13-combat:333] or [13-combat:335].

5. LOW - Near-empty page 217: after the wound table consumes p.216, only the short 'Healing Wounds' paragraph lands on p.217, leaving ~80% blank before the next forced break. Symptom of defect 1; expected to self-correct once the table flows, but should be re-checked after the fix (a keep-with-previous or break adjustment may be needed at [13-combat:318-319]).

Items verified as OK: chapter opener art (13-combat.qmd:7) renders cleanly at 60% width, no overflow (p.200); the placeholder midpoint figure (13-combat.qmd:337) renders as intended, pending final art; callout boxes at [13-combat:41], [13-combat:83], [13-combat:443] render with icon and title intact; zero em-dashes in the chapter, consistent with the book's em-dash law; heading hierarchy is otherwise consistent (all sections h2, sub-headings h3, no skipped levels once defect 3 is fixed).

evidence.claim: Render analysis of the 2026-08-25 build output: on PDF p.216 the four final rows of the wound table (566-599 through 666) print as one overlapping, clipped band at the page foot, with the centered page folio overprinting the table; none of the four rows is legible. Confirmed both visually (page raster) and by raw text extraction, which shows the row labels and effect text interleaved in the same band.

Root cause of the wound-table failure: the theme's show rule wraps every table in an unbreakable block, so an oversized table cannot split across pages and instead overruns and clips at the page bottom. The file's own comment says header rows should repeat on page breaks, but the wrapper makes that impossible - the comment and the code contradict each other.

Render analysis: every one of the chapter's four table captions prints a doubled number, the auto-generated chapter-prefixed number followed by the author's hard-coded one, e.g. the wound table caption on p.216 and the maneuvers table caption on p.204 both show two 'Table' numbers side by side.

Source location of the doubled-caption defect: the wound table caption line hard-codes its own 'Table 13.4:' label while also carrying the crossref id that drives auto-numbering; the same pattern occurs on the three other table caption lines (51, 147, 162).

Render analysis: PDF p.207 begins with the section title printed as plain body text with visible hash marks, in the same size and weight as the paragraph copy below it - not a styled heading. The Chapter 15 TOC block in the build lists sections 15.1 through 15.15 and contains no entry for Damage Types, confirming the heading was never parsed.

Source cause of the literal heading: the pagebreak directive at line 126 is immediately followed by the heading line at 127 with no blank line between them, which is why the heading syntax is not recognized as a heading.

Render analysis: PDF p.219 is a completely empty page (header and folio only), produced by two consecutive pagebreak directives in the source between the Cover section and the midpoint placeholder figure.

Render analysis: PDF p.217 holds only the short 'Healing Wounds' paragraph at the top with the rest of the page blank, a whitespace artifact downstream of the wound table overfilling p.216; flagged for re-check after the table fix.

Items verified acceptable in the build: the chapter opener image (line 7, 1024x1024 source) renders at 60% width with no overflow on p.200; the midpoint placeholder figure (line 337) renders as intended with its caption; the chapter contains no em-dashes, consistent with the standing em-dash law.

payload.argument: The round-1 disposition plan does not survive stress-testing; five of its cells fail or are incomplete. (1) Reordering the wound-table ranges cannot deliver 'every row reachable': the sorted-dice convention [13-combat:295] fixes the achievable set at 56 values, so no permutation of range endpoints can put a roll into 600-633 or 634-665 - my exhaustive enumeration shows the only achievable values at or above 500 are 555, 556, 566, 666. The carve-out cell (dedupe 222/333/555) fixes only the triple overlaps and leaves the two severest rows at zero probability; the only repair is re-labeling those rows onto 556/566, which the plan never specifies and which inverts the table's severity story: each of the two severest non-death wounds would sit at 3/216, three times likelier than 666 death at 1/216. The same enumeration shows a naive numeric split like '200-221' contains zero achievable rolls (the smallest 2xx is 222), and rows 266-299 and 366-432 each hold exactly one achievable value, so the plan's edits must be done in achievable-value space, not numeric space, and no such method is given. (2) Capping Deep Gash bleed [13-combat:306] does not close the death-engine hole: the tick fires at the start of every turn, at 0 HP the victim is Incapacitated and cannot self-bind, the death-save table promises stability on Standard [13-combat:283], and no rule anywhere defines damage at 0 HP - the cap converts an uncapped spiral into an indefinite 0-HP limbo whose only exits are a 1/216 fumble or an ally's action, while the 666 row's no-survival-rolls promise [13-combat:315] is untouched; the fix requires a bleed-at-0-HP ruling that the plan's design-decision list omits. (3) The worked-example cell corrects damage numbers, but the Gust break is an effect-tier error: the beat knocks the cultist Prone on a Standard result [13-combat:353] and builds a stand-up beat on it [13-combat:377]; re-scoping the effect to a push removes the only justification for the broken chant, since the shared-effects table defines Push as pure relocation [13-combat:151] with no casting-interruption rule, so the corrected beat needs new justification the plan does not supply; and the cell-by-cell merge leaves the summary lines [13-combat:391, 419] stale until several cells land in a specified order. (4) Removing the phantom references is a fork, not a fix: Dual Wielder is a rule conditional inside the two-weapon rules [13-combat:234], so deleting it permanently hard-gates the off-hand to the Light list while adding it would relax the rule - the plan does not choose between materially different rules; dropping Menacing Glare [13-combat:389] also deletes the chapter's only player-initiated morale demonstration, unflagged. (5) No cell addresses the Bane adjudication gap: morale is rolled with no modifiers [13-combat:254] yet the ambush imposes a DA-added Bane [13-combat:439], and the surprise-clarification cell [13-combat:124 vs 192] decides whether the surprise penalty stacks onto that same roll under the 'first round' reading - an unresolved interaction the plan treats as two independent wording cells. Finally, the breakable-table cell will expose the dead wound rows to every reader, coupling a mechanical cell to a substantive one. Tested the stand-up-cost, surprise-wording, caption, blank-line, and pagebreak cells as well: those hold as worded, but the five failures above keep the plan from being complete or correct.

payload.argument: Round 2 retest: my position holds and I confirm the corrected totals end-to-end, but I concede one fix is incomplete and name one new break. CONCESSION: my round-1 wound-table fix (exclude the triple rows from the ranges) is superseded - a full enumeration of the 56 achievable D666 outcomes shows the ranges 600-633 and 634-665 contain zero realizable rolls, so the two most severe non-fatal wounds are dead rows; the fix must remap the top of the table, not just carve out 222/333/555. RETEST vs author's plate-DR drift (4 vs 6): it changes NO worked-example total I verified - both blows on the Knight are 4, and 4 minus 4 or minus 6 floors to the stated minimum of 1 either way; the drift is real (bestiary and example agree with each other, both contradict the armor chapter) but it is example-neutral, while the buckler drift is not: with +1 instead of +2, the defender's total DR is 3, so the corrected 9-point knight blow deals 6 and the Blade ends round 1 at 5 HP (not 10), and the corrected 4-point dark bolt leaves the Odd at 6 (not 7); lines 391 and 419 must carry 5 and 6. NEW BREAK with counter-example: the two-weapon rule requires both attacks on one roll and its example uses exactly one roll, but the basic melee card prints flat 1/2/3 per tier with no sub-tier row to drop into - a Weak primary result leaves the off-hand column with no defined value (the table's bare '1 damage' cell is the only number, and nothing says whether the ability modifier rides on it or whether it is a flat floor). No finding is withdrawn: Knight Standard 9, Dark Bolt 4, Gust's Prone only on Strong, the triple stand-up prices, the surprise first-roll vs first-round split, the cover double-implementation, and the three phantom cards all stand as round 1.

evidence.claim: Worked math re-verified in round 2: the corrected knight blow of 9 against total defense value 3 yields 6, dropping the Blade from 11 to 5 HP; the corrected bolt of 4 against unarmored defense leaves the Odd at 6; the two blows the party lands on the knight (4 and 4) floor to 1 whether its armor is rated 4 or 6, so the plate rating drift does not change those totals.

D666 enumeration over all 56 achievable sorted three-dice outcomes: rows 200-265, 300-365, 500-565 each contain a separately listed triple (222, 333, 555), and rows 600-633 and 634-665 contain no achievable roll at all - my round-1 carve-out fix is incomplete because the severed top rows would remain unreachable.

The two-weapon table pairs every primary tier with an off-hand tier one step down, but the basic melee card the example uses has flat per-tier damage and no lower row, so a Weak primary result leaves the off-hand cell with no defined damage value and an undefined modifier question.
The example's off-hand attack adds the strength modifier to a finesse property weapon; the equipment chapter assigns agility to that property, so the two-blade total should be 6, not the 5 printed.

Rising from prone is priced three different ways inside the same chapter - a maneuver in one table, a move in the conditions table, and half of the movement resource in the example - so the Gust knockdown beat, which depends on that cost, has no stable price even after the spell's tier is fixed.

The defense modifier table lists the ambush penalty as first round only while the surprise section and the glossary scope it to the first roll; since the players make defense rolls too, the two scopes assign the penalty to different sets of rolls.

payload.rationale: Topic t-01 - does ch13 (Combat) hold as written - was tested by seven independent lenses (game-architect, author, editor-in-chief, layout-expert, researcher, contrarian, librarian) across two rounds, producing 14 findings (f-001 through f-014), every one a refute. The chapter's core defects are provable, not stylistic: the wound table is provably unrollable - exhaustive D666 enumeration (f-009, f-012, f-014) shows only 56 achievable outcomes, with 600-633 and 634-665 containing zero achievable rolls and 222/333/555 each claimed by two rows; the flagship worked example misnumbers NPC damage against the bestiary (Knight Standard 3 against a 6/9/12 longsword, Dark Bolt 3 against a 2/4/6 budget, Gust Standard granting Prone that its card reserves for Strong) and its HP ledger ripples through the summaries (f-002, f-003, f-010, f-014); three cards it cites (Flurry, Menacing Glare, Dual Wielder) exist nowhere in the book (f-003, f-004, f-010, f-011); and the built PDF clips the worst four wound rows into one overlapping, folio-overprinted band on p.216 because the theme wraps every table in an unbreakable block (f-005, f-013). Round 2 re-verification confirmed every round-1 refutation with no member persuading any other to drop a finding (f-008 through f-014), and the contrarian's stress test sharpened rather than rescued the plan - notably proving the wound table needs a full remap, not a carve-out (f-009). No member supported the status quo in either round (7-0 refute in both), so the council rejected rather than approved: the engine's rejected state (refute 7 >= reject_quorum 4) closed the deliberation directly, with no blind-judge ruling required.
payload.recommendation: REJECT. ch13 (Combat) does not hold as written and must not be published until the disposition plan below is executed and re-verified in a clean build. (a) Mechanical fixes (safe micro-PR sweep): (1) re-derive the wound-table ranges onto the 56 achievable D666 outcomes and add a stated precedence rule so no roll matches two entries (222/333/555 are each claimed by two rows, and 600-633/634-665 contain no achievable roll at all); (2) split the wound table into two parts with repeated headers, or replace the theme's unbreakable table wrapper with a breakable one, so the table renders (the built PDF clips the worst four rows on p.216); (3) delete the hard-coded 'Table 13.x:' prefixes so Quarto's auto-numbering is the sole label (doubled captions on all four tables); (4) unify the stand-up-from-prone cost across the basic-maneuvers table, the conditions table, and the worked example (currently Maneuver / movement / half movement); (5) unify the surprise wording to first roll across the modifiers table, the surprise section, and the glossary; (6) state the minimum-1 damage floor after armor as an explicit rule instead of only showing it in the example; (7) demote the three callout-wrapped H2 headings (lines 42, 84, 444) to H3 or bold so they stop polluting the TOC; (8) delete one of the double pagebreaks at lines 333/335 that inject an orphan blank page; (9) make '## Damage Types' parse as a heading (blank line after the pagebreak at line 126, currently the only one of eighteen without one) so it returns to the TOC; (10) excise the draft residue 'but wait, Kael is only Adept' at line 411; (11) fix the art caption format (stale placeholder descriptor naming a nonexistent unit). (b) Substantive cross-chapter reconciliation (dispatched pass): (1) rewrite the worked example so every NPC figure matches the authoritative sources - Knight longsword Standard 3 to 9, Cultist Dark Bolt 3 to 4, Gust Standard is a 10 ft push not Prone - and re-derive the shared party HP ledger and summary lines as one atomic edit (Kael to 5 HP, Lyra to 6 HP); (2) resolve the three phantom cards cited but defined nowhere in the book (Flurry, Menacing Glare, Dual Wielder) by adding them or replacing the affected beats with existing cards; (3) reconcile equipment DR drift: buckler +2 in the example vs +1 in the armor/equipment chapters, and plate DR 4 in the example and bestiary vs DR 6 in the armor chapter; (4) eliminate the double implementation of Cover (defense bonus +1/+3 in one place, attacker penalty -1/-3 in another, with no cross-reference); (5) define the off-hand weapon's ability modifier for Finesse weapons (Agility, not Brawn); (6) define the Choke/suffocation state and its endpoint, which no chapter currently defines; (7) cap Deep Gash bleed-out and state its behavior at 0 HP; (8) state how Bane stacks when multiple sources apply. (c) Design decisions for Bruce (flag veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md): (1) whether defense rolls get Critical/Fumble overrides (the attack and death-save tables have them, the defense table does not); (2) the mapping of fractional Challenge values to modifiers; (3) Deep Gash bleed at 0 HP (the death-save table's stability promise contradicts an unbound bleed); (4) wound-table top-end lethality, since any re-map puts the two severest non-death rows at 3/216, three times likelier than the 1/216 death row.

resolved.outcome: ch13 (Combat) was reviewed by the hol-rulebook council (7 lenses, 2 rounds, 14 findings, all refute) and REJECTED as written: the engine's rejected state holds (refute 7 >= reject_quorum 4), so no blind-judge ruling was required; the chapter must not be published until the disposition plan attached in the recommendation - mechanical micro-PR sweep, substantive cross-chapter reconciliation, and the four design decisions for Bruce - is executed and re-verified in a clean build.
